title: Add multi-AZ VPC control plane Terraform module with advanced peering, endpoints, SGs and Route53 DNS
author: Priya Nair
description: This PR introduces a production-ready Terraform module to provision the VPC control plane used by Redwood Private deployments across multiple availability zones. Motivation: customers deploying Private control planes in regulated environments requested a repeatable, audited, multi-AZ topology with managed interface endpoints, secure peering to customer VPCs, and Route53 private hosted zone peering for DNS resolution. Changes include: new module 'vpc-control-plane' with configurable AZ count, public/private subnets, NAT gateways, managed VPC endpoints for S3/ECR/SSM/STS, security groups with least-privilege rules for control plane components, cross-account/region VPC peering helper, Route53 resolver and private hosted zone peering configuration, outputs for control-plane endpoint IPs and peering IDs, and example usage with variables and a README. Implementation notes: defaults favor 3 AZs, single NAT per AZ with optional central NAT option, endpoints created when enable_endpoints=true, security groups separate control-plane internal and bastion access, IAM policy document examples for peering acceptance, and automated DNS delegation via route53 vpc_association_authorization. This PR also includes integration tests (terraform-integration) and a migration guide for existing customers to adopt the module. Checklist: [x] Terraform module and examples added; [x] Unit/format checks; [x] Integration tests (initial run passed on AWS us-east-1); [x] Docs/README and upgrade notes; [x] Security review with SG rules and IAM templates. Breaking changes: none to existing modules; the module is additive. Related: ENG-2113 (private control plane delivery), SUP-3398 (customer request for multi-AZ peering).
